Implementation Plan

**Implementation plan for #6459: heal-evidence logs leak `Authorization: Basic` headers and step env values**

Planning ref: `claude/heal-evidence-bundle` @ `182cebe4f983081f7f4f5fd979df1470fef5a2b0`. This matches the issue's integration-branch metadata, so there is no mismatch.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends redact_secrets
Scope-mode justification: The finding asks for two things. Basic authorization headers must be redacted, and environment values must be kept out of the logs the agents read, failing closed. Both fixes belong in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`. They extend the existing `_SECRET_RES` / `redact_secrets` list and the `slice_job_log` pass instead of adding a new component. The plan goes slightly past the finding in one place: logs already collected and cached would still hold env values, so the cache-reuse check gets a format marker that forces a re-fetch. That costs about 15 extra lines and no new dependency or interface. The Boil the Lake rule applies, and correctness ranks above speed (§6). I left `filter_log` in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py` alone on purpose. Changing what it outputs would change failure fingerprints and break de-duplication of existing heal lineages. The module docstring already says it is unchanged for that reason.

**Automation / wiring (§20.E)**
- No new script, supervisor or scheduler wiring; this only changes existing code.
- Callers that pick up the fix with no change of their own:
  - the `collect` path that clarify, plan and implement use for heal issues;
  - the `slice-log` call in `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:250`.
- No database work and no entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

---

**1. Files likely to change**
- `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`: the main fix.
- `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py`: update one existing assertion and add regression tests.
- `agents.md` (around line 211, the slice-log description "the failing step's env"): say that env values are omitted.
- `changelog.d/6459-heal-evidence-env-redaction.md`: new fragment, `<!-- changelog: security -->` or `fixed`, following CLAUDE.md §20.

**2. Functions / modules**

a) **Basic and other authorization-scheme redaction.** Add patterns to `_SECRET_RES` (around line 155). Keep the existing Bearer/token pattern exactly as it is so its output (`Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]`) stays the same.
- New pattern: `(?i)\b((?:proxy-)?authorization["']?\s*[:=]\s*["']?basic\s+)(?!\[REDACTED\])[^\s"']+`.
  - Group 1 keeps the prefix, so the existing `m.group(1) + "[REDACTED]"` branch in `redact_secrets` handles it.
  - `\b` before `authorization` also matches `Proxy-Authorization`.
  - The `(?!\[REDACTED\])` lookahead makes the pattern safe to apply twice.
- Fail-closed catch-all: one more pattern that redacts the value of any `authorization:` / `authorization=` header whose scheme is not bearer/token/basic (for example digest or negotiate), or that has no scheme at all.
  - It must never re-redact `[REDACTED]`. Use a negative lookahead on `(?:bearer|token|basic)\s` and on `\[REDACTED\]`.
  - Lines the earlier patterns already rewrote must come out unchanged.
- The patterns match case-insensitively. That covers the `actions/checkout` form `http.https://github.com/.extraheader AUTHORIZATION: basic <b64>`.

b) **Strip env values.** New private helper `_omit_step_env_values(lines: list[str]) -> list[str]`. I checked that the name is not already used in the module.
- It runs inside `slice_job_log` on `content` right after `heal.sanitize_text`, before any section is built. So the error windows, the env section, diagnostics and the tail all see the reduced text, not only the env section.
- Inside a `##[group]Run ` header block (`_STEP_RUN_HEADER_RE`), after an `env:` line, every indented line is rewritten:
  - `  NAME: value` becomes `  NAME: [value omitted]`, with NAME matching `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`.
  - Any indented line that does not parse as a name/value pair, such as a multi-line value continuation, becomes `    [env line omitted]`.
- The env block ends at `##[endgroup]`, at the first line that is not indented, or at a new `##[group]` line.
  - A log truncated in the middle of an env block therefore has every remaining indented line reduced. That is the fail-closed requirement.
- Diagnostic exception, kept for #6055: values are kept only for names in a new constant `_ENV_VALUE_KEEP_NAMES = frozenset({"GIT_DIR", "GIT_WORK_TREE"})`, and only when the value fully matches `^/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]{1,300}$`, an absolute path made of safe characters. Anything else is still omitted.
- `with:` input blocks are not changed. See D2.
- Update the `slice_job_log` docstring and the module docstring (line 11): "the env variable names (values omitted) of the step that raised the first error".

c) **Invalidate stale cached logs.** Job logs collected before this fix still contain env values.
- Add a constant `LOG_SLICE_FORMAT = "env-values-omitted.v1"`, next to `ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_FORMAT`.
- `collect_run` writes `meta["log_slice_format"] = LOG_SLICE_FORMAT`.
- The cached-reuse branch reuses a run only when `cached.get("log_slice_format") == LOG_SLICE_FORMAT`, in addition to the existing artifact-format condition.
- On a mismatch, before re-fetching, delete every `job-*.txt` under `self.out / run_dir`. This runs together with the existing `_clear_artifact_dirs(run_dir)` call. If a re-fetch then returns `log_unavailable`, no pre-fix log is left behind, and the existing `_skip(..., "log_unavailable")` records it.

**3. Data structures affected**
- `meta.json` per run gets one new key, `log_slice_format`. This is additive; older meta files without it are treated as stale and re-collected.
- The sliced-log text format changes: env values are replaced with `[value omitted]`. Section headings stay the same.

**4. API / interface changes**
- The CLI is unchanged: `slice-log`, `collect` and `prompt-section` keep the same arguments. `redact_secrets` keeps its signature.
- No new GitHub API calls. Cache invalidation costs one-time re-fetches using the calls `collect_run` already makes, bounded by the existing per-run job limit and rate-limit guard (§14).

## Decisions

### D1 — Omit env values in the sliced log instead of just running secret regexes over them
- Chosen: rewrite every `env:` entry inside a step header to `NAME: [value omitted]`, failing closed on lines that do not parse, and keep values only for an allowlist of path-valued git variables.
- Alternatives considered: only add more secret regexes (keeps values and misses unknown credential shapes); drop the env section entirely (loses the variable names that diagnoses rely on).
- Why: the finding asks to omit env values and to fail closed. An allowlist is safe even for credential shapes we do not know. Variable names and the two git path variables keep the #6055 diagnosis possible.

### D2 — Leave `with:` inputs unchanged
- Chosen: reduce only the `env:` blocks. `with:` values still pass through `redact_secrets`, including the new Basic pattern.
- Alternatives considered: omit `with:` values as well.
- Why: the finding is about the env block. GitHub masks secret-backed `with:` inputs (`***`), and inputs such as `ref:` and `fetch-depth:` are useful for diagnosis. The Basic and catch-all patterns still catch a header written into an input. Recorded as a warning below.

### D3 — Force re-collection through a log-format marker
- Chosen: add `LOG_SLICE_FORMAT` to `meta.json`, re-collect on mismatch, and delete stale `job-*.txt` files first.
- Alternatives considered: rely on readers applying `redact_secrets` again (it does not remove env values); purge the whole evidence directory (wasteful and loses artifacts that are fine).
- Why: this is the same pattern as `ARTIFACT_EXTRACT_FORMAT`. Without it, `complete` cached runs would keep serving logs with env values in them.

### D4 — Do not change `filter_log`
- Chosen: no change to `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`.
- Alternatives considered: apply the same env reduction to `filter_log`.
- Why: the fingerprint comes from `filter_log`. Changing its output would split existing lineages and dedupe keys. Its Basic-header exposure is outside the finding's location. Recorded as a warning.

## Security considerations
- **Trust boundary.** The raw Actions job logs are untrusted and are fetched with `GH_PAT` in a trusted step. The sliced output becomes input for model prompts: it is mounted read-only at `/evidence` for clarify, and the intake diagnosis prompt uses it. It can then end up in issue or PR comments. Credentials must be removed before the write, inside `slice_job_log` and `_write` / `redact_secrets`, not by the readers.
- **Authorization.** No new endpoint or surface. `collect` keeps its existing eligibility and provenance checks.
- **Input validation.**
  - Env-block detection uses only the header markers the sanitized log already contains.
  - The allowlisted value must match a strict absolute-path regex.
  - The redaction patterns are anchored and use bounded character classes. Avoid nested quantifiers that could backtrack catastrophically.
- **Abuse cases.**
  - (a) A step env carries `AUTH: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz`: the env value is omitted and Basic is redacted elsewhere.
  - (b) A malicious step prints `Authorization: Basic <b64>` in its output, which then lands in an error window or the tail: the Basic pattern redacts it.
  - (c) A log truncated mid-env, or a value continued across lines: every remaining indented line is reduced.
  - (d) An attacker controls `GIT_WORK_TREE` and sets it to something like `/tmp/x ghp_...`: the space fails the path regex, so the value is omitted.
  - (e) A cached pre-fix log: the format mismatch triggers a purge and re-fetch.
- No secrets end up in code, logs or tests. Test fixtures use synthetic base64.
